scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The lion dance originated outside China, likely from India or Persia, and was introduced to China via Central Asia.
The earliest Chinese references date back to the Han dynasty, with detailed descriptions appearing in the Tang dynasty.
The Southern Lion dance, which predominates in Malaysia, developed later in Guangdong province and is linked to myths such as the monster Nian.
on_screen: Map: Malaysia · Southeast Asia

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: The lion dance is performed to bring good luck, fortune, and to ward off evil spirits.
It is a central feature of Lunar New Year celebrations and is also performed at weddings, business openings, and to honor special guests.
The dance symbolizes strength, courage, and auspiciousness, rooted in local myths such as the defeat of the monster Nian.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The Southern Lion dance is performed by two dancers: one manipulating the head and the other the tail of the lion costume.
The dance involves acrobatic movements, mimicking the lion's expressions and gestures, often synchronized with vigorous drumbeats, gongs, and cymbals.
The dance includes playful and martial elements, with movements inspired by kung fu.
Watch for Lion's blink, Lion's roar, Acrobatic leap.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: The Southern Lion costume features a large head made of papier-mâché over a bamboo frame, decorated with fur and painted designs, including a single horn.
The body is a durable cloth trimmed with fur, often with a long tail attached.
Performances typically occur during Lunar New Year, weddings, business openings, and cultural festivals, often outdoors or in community halls.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Feng Gengzhang founded the Hok San style of Southern Lion dance, refining the lion's movements to resemble a cat and redesigning the lion head.
Li Yi Sheng introduced Hok San style to Singapore and Malaysia in the 1920s, founding the Singapore Hok San Association Lion Dance Troupe.
The Southern Lion dance in Malaysia is mainly derived from the Guangdong styles, including Fut San and Hok San.
The Malaysian Southern Lion dance traces its lineage to the Guangdong province of China, brought by Chinese immigrants.

scenes.title: Family tree
narration: Malaysian dance is parent of Chinese lion dance: Malaysian Southern Lion dance derives directly from Chinese Southern Lion traditions.
Malaysian dance is sibling of Northern Lion dance: Northern Lion is a distinct Chinese style less common in Malaysia.
Malaysian dance is shares music of Vietnamese lion dance: Vietnamese lion dance shares Chinese origins and percussion styles.
Malaysian dance is shares music of Japanese shishi-mai: Japanese lion dance shares cultural roots but differs in style and instrumentation.
